g.bits: a bit = the surprise of one fair coin flip.
g.pastonly: past-only model: it learns from plays before the weeks it guesses, so it never sees the answer ahead of time.
g.bracket: the bracket [a, b]: the log resampled in four-week blocks and recounted many times; 95 of 100 recounts land inside.
g.prereg: pre-registered: the test and its pass bar were written down and locked before the data was looked at.
g.failcond: failure conditions: three findings, named in advance, that would undo the result if they ever turned up.
g.insample: in-sample: measured on the same plays it was found in. not yet checked on plays it never saw.
g.heldout: held out: plays hidden from the model while it learned, then used to test it. a fair exam, not a rerun.
g.direction: a direction, not a size: the sign is trusted (mine goes farther), the amount is not certified.
g.bridge: bridge index: how often my press lands in another family, over how often the queue's step does. above 1 = mine more.
g.clap: CLAP: an open model that listens to audio and turns it into numbers; sounds it hears as alike get alike numbers.
g.umap: UMAP: a way to squeeze many numbers per artist down to two or three axes, keeping near things near.
g.mert: MERT: a second open audio model, trained on music. it checks CLAP's direction; it does not confirm it.
g.soundmap: the sound map: every artist placed by how its previews sound to the model. near = alike to the model, not to me.
g.playmap: the play-order map: artists pulled together each time one played right after the other in my log.
g.tgraph: transition graph: one dot per artist, one line each time one artist played right after another in a sitting.
g.forcelayout: force layout: linked dots pull together and every dot pushes the rest away, until the drawing settles.
g.louvain: Louvain: a standard method that splits a network into groups with more lines inside them than chance would give.
g.firstorder: first-order: built from one step back only, the artist right before. the queue's next artist depends on the last two.
g.rooms: neighborhood (room): a group of artists the log keeps playing together, found from play order alone.
g.partition: partition: one way of splitting every artist into rooms. another seed can draw a slightly different one.
g.giant: giant component: the largest connected part of the graph. artists with no path into it sit on the rim.
g.seed: seed and resolution: the random start and the grain of the grouping. change either and the rooms can shift.
g.stable: the 0.80 bar: rerun with new seeds, the rooms had to agree with themselves at least 80 in 100 to count as stable.
g.ceiling: a same-size ceiling: the most agreement groups of the same sizes could reach. without it, the score has no scale.
g.timbre: timbre measure: a hand-built number for tone color (bright, dark, rough), made without any learned model.
g.radial: radial: names on a rim grouped by family; each line bends through its two families' hubs.
g.bundled: bundled: a force layout where lines that share a route are drawn as one bundle, so the main roads show.
g.islands: constellations: one island per family. a line between islands is a step from one family to another.
g.arcs: arcs: names in one row, each step drawn as an arch above it. a long arch is a long jump.
g.run: the queue's run: the songs it plays in a row, each next to the last in sound, until something breaks the run.
g.apart: apart: how far the next song sits from the one before in the model's sound space. bigger = less alike.
g.rr: RR (rate ratio): one rate over another. 2.27 means a little more than twice as often.
g.perm: permutation p: how often shuffled labels give a gap this big by luck. under 0.0005 = almost never.
g.placebo: placebo: the same test on a fake marker. it should find nothing, and here it points the other way.
g.median: median: the middle value. half the likes land before it, half after.
g.ledger: ledger: the numbered audit trail. each row ties one claim to its script, its data and its result.
g.descriptive: descriptive: a pattern reported as seen. no pre-registered test stands behind it, so it is not a claim.
g.undetermined: undetermined: the test could not tell either way, so no direction is claimed.
g.frozen: the frozen export: the log as downloaded once and fixed. every headline number is counted on it.
g.familiarity: matched familiarity: compared only across artists i had already played about as often.
g.account: the account data: the full download spotify sends on request, including every song in my library.
g.anchor: the anchor: the pre-registered family result (ambient and lofi at 0.71) that the other genre lines lean on.
g.propagated: propagated labels: genres guessed for untagged artists from the artists they were played beside.
g.chance: chance: what a guess with no information scores. a coin picks right 50 times in 100.
g.lane: lane: one test, written down in advance, run once, then handed to a referee who tries to break it.
g.referee: adversarial referee: a separate review whose only job is to try to break the result before it goes up.
g.certified: certified: passed a test written down in advance, with its bar set before the data was seen.
g.lastfm: Last.fm: a music site where listeners tag artists. its tags name the families; Apple's genre fills the gaps.
g.family: family: a broad genre (ambient/lofi, jazz, rock/metal and so on) built from the tags listeners give each artist.
g.queue: the queue: the song that started by itself when the last one ended. nobody pressed anything. violet.
g.served: served: a play the app started on its own when the last song ended, the queue. violet.
g.shuffle: shuffle: plays started with shuffle on. i picked the list, the app picked the order. amber.
g.press: my press: a play i started myself, by tapping a song or play. mint.
g.sitting: a sitting: a run of plays with no gap longer than 30 minutes, about one listening session.
g.strict: the strictest count: only plays i started by tapping a song; skip and back presses are left out.
g.interval: interval: the range of values the data allows around a number. wide = the data cannot pin it down.
